newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to send 200 soldiers to Haiti for training.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to send 200 soldiers to Haiti for training.

text.p: The U.S. Army is sending about 200 soldiers to Haiti on Friday for a four- to seven-day training exercise unrelated to the U.N. peacekeeping mission on the island, the Defence Department said on Wednesday.

The deployment of soldiers from the Army's 82nd Airborne Division from Fort Bragg, North Carolina, is the fourth in a series of such "contingency readiness" exercises by the U.S. Atlantic Command, the Pentagon said in a statement.

"The soldiers will train to carry out contingency plans, which include the protection of U.S. forces conducting humanitarian civic assistance projects in Haiti," it said. "These soldiers are not part of the U.N. mission, nor is their mandate to provide a secure and stable environment in Haiti."
There are about 480 U.S. military personnel on Haiti, including a headquarters of about 90 and units involved in engineering, medical and security force training, the Pentagon said.

About 1,300 U.N. peacekeepers stationed on Haiti are scheduled to leave on July 31, although Canada, which provides 736 of the troops, last week said its soldiers would stay until the end of the year.
The United Nations took over peacekeeping in Haiti in March 1995.
